clue.text: Being the leading player, Edward began

parts.note: to be the leading player in a show is to be its star
Ted is a familiar short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A man called Edward started out by taking the lead role.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin something is to set it going, so began and started are synonyms.

clue.text: Spot non-drinking egghead getting involved in dispute

indicators.note: getting involved in a thing means going into it, so these letters are placed within the other piece

parts.note: to spar is to argue or dispute
TT is short for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol
the head, or first letter, of the word egg is E

explanation.surface: A teetotal intellectual gets caught up in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like a brainy person, but it gives only the first letter of 'egg'; 'getting involved in' puts the teetotal letters and that E inside the dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatter is a small splash or mark, which is a spot.

clue.text: The dolt goes around doing nothing without assistance

indicators.note: one piece going around another wraps it, so the letters for dolt surround the rest

parts.note: an ass is a stupid person, a dolt
someone idle is doing nothing

explanation.surface: A lazy fool wanders about with nobody helping him.
explanation.definitionFit: An aid is a help, so to be aidless is to be without help or support.

clue.text: Sort of health-worker to join the strike first

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply, as on a door
1st is written out as IST, the I standing for the figure one

explanation.surface: A medical worker is urged to be first to join the walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it means to hit (RAP). 'First' is the abbreviation 1st, with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A counsellor or physiotherapist is a kind of practitioner treating patients, a type of health professional.

clue.text: Seaside accommodation giving rise to complaint

indicators.note: accommodation can mean adjustment or rearrangement, so the letters of the word before are reorganised

explanation.surface: Lodgings by the sea leave a guest ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accommodation' looks like a seaside guesthouse but signals that the letters of SEASIDE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Living where it's bracing

explanation.surface: A resort is recommended because the air there is invigorating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bracing' suggests fresh sea air, but stays are the ropes or struts that brace a mast or a corset.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying somewhere means residing or lodging there; and staying is the set of supports, ropes or struts that brace a structure.

clue.text: Bearing the right credit-notes is important

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass bearing
IOUs are written promises to pay, notes of credit

explanation.surface: Holding the proper IOUs matters a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like 'carrying', but it is a compass direction, here SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serious is weighty and significant, much as an important matter is.

clue.text: Strange article about a deliberately misleading story

indicators.note: about here means round the outside, so the article encloses the other piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a lie is an intentionally false tale

explanation.surface: An odd newspaper piece concerns a made-up tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign or unfamiliar, so it can mean odd or peculiar.

clue.text: Check when a little crawler takes in cash

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so the crawler's letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: an insect is a small creeping creature
P, for penny or pence, stands for a small sum of money

explanation.surface: A bug swallows some coins while being examined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like a bank cheque in a clue about cash, but it is the definition, meaning examine.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to examine it closely, the same as to scrutinise it.

clue.text: More exalted old monarch — a scoffer

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, refers to one of the past King Georges
to scoff is British slang for to eat greedily, so a scoffer is an eater

explanation.surface: A former king turns out to be a mocker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffer' looks like someone who mocks, but in British slang to scoff is to wolf food down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more exalted is grander or higher in rank, a comparative of great.

clue.text: Making a note to prepare a speech

parts.note: D is one of the notes of the musical scale
to dress food is to prepare it, as with a salad or a chicken

explanation.surface: Someone jots a reminder to get ready for giving a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk delivered to an audience is an oration or speech.

clue.text: Relating to one's children, get put out again

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
issue is a formal word for offspring

explanation.surface: A matter about one's offspring gets published a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Children' gives ISSUE, a legal word for descendants.
explanation.definitionFit: To republish a book or stamp is to bring it out once more.

clue.text: A Greek character at the exchange

indicators.note: exchange means swapping places, so the letters of the two words before trade positions

explanation.surface: A Greek person is spotted at the stock exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange' looks like a place of trade, but it signals that the letters of 'at the' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth letter of the Greek alphabet is one of its characters.

clue.text: Decorating which puts navy personnel in a spot

indicators.note: in places one piece within another, so the navy personnel sit inside a spot

parts.note: a dot is a small spot
RN is the Royal Navy
men are staff or personnel

explanation.surface: Sailors are posted to a particular place to dress it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Adornment is the act of decorating, embellishing something to make it attractive.

clue.text: Wild spree — it makes a break!

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the next words run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A frantic binge lets someone get away from routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a pause or rest from something hard, an interval of relief.

clue.text: Putting a point to a club, fail to express oneself clearly

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
a putter is a golf club used on the green

explanation.surface: A golfer getting the ball close to the flag starts to stammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point (S), and 'club' a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: To sputter is to speak in a hasty, spluttering way, failing to talk clearly.

clue.text: Insufficiently experienced support basically

parts.note: under as a prefix means too little or not enough
to have felt something is to have experienced it

explanation.surface: A new recruit is not sufficiently seasoned to back anybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support basically' is the definition: underlay lies at the base of a carpet, supporting it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is felt laid beneath a carpet as underlay, a support at floor level.

clue.text: He'll find the top man comes in later

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the letters of the other word

parts.note: OC, officer commanding, is the man in charge of a unit

explanation.surface: The boss shows up late to the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top man' gives OC, the Officer Commanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who locates things is a finder, a person who tracks them down.

clue.text: Generous politician?

explanation.surface: A big-spending member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal means giving freely, open-handed; it also names a member of the Liberal party in politics.

clue.text: Guys a writer

parts.note: a chap is a guy, a fellow
a man is also a guy or bloke

explanation.surface: Some fellows are a single author.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'Guys', supplies two pieces: CHAP and MAN, both words for a fellow. George Chapman was an Elizabethan playwright and translator of Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Chapman was an English dramatist and poet, so he is an author.

clue.text: Dealing with a negotiator employed by chemists

parts.note: re means concerning or dealing with
an agent negotiates deals on someone's behalf

explanation.surface: Talks with a broker are hired by the pharmacy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a substance used in laboratory tests to produce a reaction, a tool of chemistry.

clue.text: Scroungers — there are many different grades

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters of the next word are put in a new order

explanation.surface: There are many separate levels of ability on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives C, the Roman 100.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cadges begs or sponges off others, so cadgers are spongers.

clue.text: The song of a sea-nymph

explanation.surface: A tune sung by a mermaid.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a style of West Indian ballad music; and it is also the nymph who held Odysseus on her island in Homer.

clue.text: People could come to some harm by the look of it

definitions.text: People could come to some harm by the look of it

parts.words: People could come to some harm by the look of it
parts.note: a superstition holds that a malevolent glare can bring misfortune, so harm comes literally from a look

explanation.surface: Things look dangerous for the people involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the look of it' seems to mean 'apparently', but read literally it is a harmful look.
explanation.definitionFit: A malevolent stare believed to cause injury or bad luck to whoever receives it.

clue.text: There's possibly about fifty in the refuge

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
possibly suggests the letters could take another form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, its six letters including the S
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Around fifty people are perhaps in the safe house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges THERE'S into SHETER, and 'about' puts it round L (fifty), giving SHE-L-TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a place of safety or protection from danger, a haven.

clue.text: Crime associated with Edward III's eldest son?

definitions.text: Crime associated with Edward III's eldest son?

parts.words: Crime associated with Edward III's eldest son?
parts.note: Edward III's eldest son was known as the Black Prince, said to wear dark armour, and chain armour is called mail

explanation.surface: A historian asks what offence the heir of a medieval king committed.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward the Black Prince's armour would be black mail, which as one word is the crime of extortion.
explanation.definitionFit: This is extortion: demanding payment under threat of exposing someone's secrets.

clue.text: The rascal wanted to play

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'The rascal wanted to play' (5): 'The rascal' defines KNAVE, but no parse of 'wanted to play' gives KNAVE and a search of the exact text found no explanation

clue.text: Grow a little house-plant — the aspidistra is easiest

indicators.note: a little means only a small part, so a short run of letters is taken from the following words

explanation.surface: Of all small indoor plants, the aspidistra is the easiest to cultivate.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'aspidistRA IS Easiest'.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise plants or animals is to rear or cultivate them, to bring them up.

clue.text: Go on about a member's disturbing behaviour

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to go on angrily is to rage or rant
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician who keeps ranting behaves in an unsettling way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on' reads as 'continue', but here it means to rant furiously; 'about' wraps that word round A and the Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of violent, unruly conduct, a frenzied riot.

clue.text: On the quiet some soldiers posted a donation

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
something posted has been sent by mail

explanation.surface: Some troops discreetly mailed a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is a gift, something given freely, like a donation.

clue.text: Clement backed a German put inside fast!

indicators.note: put inside means one piece is inserted into the other

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

indicators.note: backed means the letters of that German word run in reverse

parts.note: ein is German for a

explanation.surface: Clement supported a German who was quickly jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clement' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning merciful. 'Backed' turns the German word into NIE, which 'put inside' places within the fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement means merciful or mild, as a forgiving judge or gentle weather is.

clue.text: A coat that will last longer?

explanation.surface: A shopper asks which jacket will be the most durable.
explanation.walkthrough: As a noun it reads as outerwear, a coat; as a verb it means to outlast.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer garments such as a jacket are worn outside; and to outlive something in use is to keep going beyond it.
